statement: For every integer R>=5, let j_R=11*2^(R-4)-5. This is an actual odd K4,r9 member and its first nonnegative-surplus rank is exactly rho(j_R)=R+1. Indeed B_5<2^11 and B_(n+1)<B_n^2 give B_R^2<2^(11*2^(R-4))<q_(j_R), forcing strict canonicality and negative surplus through rank R. At rank R+1, the first-wall branch is strictly positive by the audited round-eight arbitrary-carry theorem, while in the stable branch B_(R+2)>=2^(2+2^R)>2048q_(j_R) and the ratio cone force D_(R+1)>4q_(j_R). Moreover 2^(R-1)<j_R+4<2^R, so the round-nine bound is p(j_R)=R+2. Thus the memberwise O(log j)=O(log log q_j) recovery upper rate is asymptotically sharp and has additive gap one on this explicit infinite subsequence.
